content:
monitoring-bot: PAGER: High error rate (502/RESET) observed on PrivateLink endpoints serving customer ACME in az-f (us-west-azf). Alert shows DNS NXDOMAIN spike and route withdraws. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/privconnect/azf-evictions

alice: seeing the same. errors started ~3951234500. I'm on it. @ben can you grab BGP view?

ben: ack. pulling RIB now. flaps from peer 10.20.3.1 -> AS64512. Noticed route withdraws at 3951234498. putting snippet:
```
BGP> show ip bgp 10.238.0.0/20
Status: Withdrawn -> Re-advertised
Paths: 1: 64512 64513
Last update: 2024-11-22T12:15:10Z
``` 

carlos: customer reports Private DNS for privatelink.acme.internal sometimes returns AZ-scoped CNAME that points to an ENI that gets evicted shortly after. NXDOMAIN and negative cache counts up ~1800/min.

dana: customer-eng on call. ACME says retries are failing — their client is sticky to AZ resolution. They see failover to public endpoint succeed but it's slower and impacts latency. Logs: `connection reset by peer` from private ENI.

alice: immediate mitigation: shift route policy for ACME's CIDR to prefer region-wide VIP (global-prvlink) until we fix ENI eviction. Pushing via rtrctl now.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook: privatelink-az-eviction -> actions: 1) shift-policy 2) disable-AZ-affinity 3) notify-customer 4) monitor-dns

ben: policy pushed: `rtrctl set policy acme-prv prefer=global-prvlink priority=200` — propagation ok in ~10s.

alice: can someone validate DNS resolution after policy change? run `dig +short privatelink.acme.internal @10.2.0.2` from a vpc host.

carlos: before: `vpce-azf-1234.acme.local` -> ENI 10.238.3.12 (dead)
after: `vpce-usw-regional` -> 10.238.1.1 (healthy)

customer-eng: ACME confirms error rate dropped to baseline after ~30s. They will hold on failover while we investigate root cause. Thx.

ben: digging into control-plane logs — there was a flurry of ENI detach events correlating with autoscale jobs at 3951234485. Working with infra to see if autoscaler issued detach before route withdraw.

dana: I'll open a support ticket with infra and CC ACME. Also preparing a short customer note: brief private endpoint disruption, automatic failover applied, no data loss, next update in 30m.

alice: handing off to @ben for investigation (oncall shift) — I'm ~30m out. ben, please take primary. :arrow_right:

ben: taking. will loop in infra and cloud-provider for ENI detach reason. starting full audit and BGP graph.

sre-runbook-bot: Incident state: mitigation-applied. Impact: partial automated failover to global endpoint. Pager resolved. Severity: Sev2. Next update at 3951234800.

dana: all comms saved to incident doc: https://internal.incidents/3951234567

customer-eng: ACME appreciates quick response. They'll run longer regression tests tonight and report back.

ben: initial hypothesis: autoscaler race condition + route reflection timing -> short-lived routes caused DNS to point clients at an ENI that was being detached. TTLs (30s) combined with negative caching amplified errors. Plan: add a guard to prevent ENI detach until route-withdrawal confirmation, and temporarily bump negative TTL for privatelink zone while we roll a fix.

alice: agreed. creating follow-ups in PM board and scheduling infra sync. closing immediate page but keeping channel open for updates.

monitoring-bot: NOTE: alert suppressed for 10m for this incident to avoid noise.
